open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input
open_points.text: “module:surface turns every JSON text a request carries … into its canonical form with canonical_values.canonical_bytes” but canonical_bytes takes “One JSON value” and may refuse “a duplicate key.”
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or an already parsed value, and which layer detects duplicate object keys before parsing loses them?
options: canonical_bytes receives raw JSON text and parses it while detecting duplicates
surface parses with a duplicate-preserving parser and passes a parsed representation plus duplicate-key evidence
canonical_bytes receives ordinary parsed values, so duplicate-key refusal is impossible there
open_points.default_guess: Have canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text at the surface boundary and detect duplicate keys while parsing.

open_points.subject: authored trial-case port coverage
open_points.text: “Add an authored trial case that fits its contract version” and “input values by port, optional expected outputs” do not say whether the supplied maps must contain exactly the declared ports or may omit or add ports.
open_points.question: Must authored inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extra names, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every output or may it specify only a subset?
options: Require exact input coverage and exact output coverage whenever expected_outputs is present
Require exact inputs but allow partial expected outputs
Allow missing or extra entries and validate only entries supplied
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all input ports and, when expected_outputs is present, exactly all output ports, with no extras.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile lookup identity
open_points.text: M22 says “Substitution: equal facts are the same spooled file,” where its facts include digest, size, media type and disclosure class, while read_spooled_file says it is named only by “run_id, producer_node_id, map_index, attempt_number, producer_port, list_index” and that “its digest, size and media type are not asked.”
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile’s identity the producer-position tuple alone, or all M22 facts including content and classification?
options: Producer-position tuple alone is the lookup identity; remaining facts are record attributes
All M22 facts form the identity and must be supplied for lookup
Give SpooledFile a separate computed identifier derived from all facts
open_points.default_guess: Use the producer-position tuple alone as the unique lookup identity.

open_points.subject: store.record_change mutable fields
open_points.text: “a lifecycle change of another entity (a status, who decided or resolved or released and when, concluded_at) updates those fields of the entity's one record in place … every other field is never changed,” while named changes also update run outputs, waiting points, ended_at, cancelled_by and resumptions, plus acceptance and revocation fields.
open_points.question: What is the complete closed set of fields each mutable entity may update in place?
options: Enumerate mutable fields separately for Run, OperationBinding, EffectApproval, StandingGrant and EffectAttempt
Treat every field described by its model lifecycle as mutable
Permit each named store change to update exactly the fields listed in that change’s payload
open_points.default_guess: Define a per-model closed mutable-field list and require each named change to stay within it.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service,” although A08 rule 5 also contains operation-specific checks requiring an operation name, proposed ports and idempotency-key fields that this start operation does not receive.
open_points.question: Which exact subset of A08 rule 5 must check_installed_instances apply at startup, and does it validate every capability or only service- and instance-level structure?
options: Check only service-record parsing, service identity, capability-name uniqueness and selected-instance header facts
Validate every capability’s record-level effect class, exposure and idempotency syntax as well
Validate only the selected instance and do not inspect capabilities
open_points.default_guess: Check service-level structure, duplicate capability names and the selected instance’s required headers, without operation/proposal-specific checks.

open_points.subject: service_invoker prepared request secrecy
open_points.text: prepare_request returns “A prepared request” after resolving the credential, while State 3 says service_invoker withholds credential echoes “since only it holds the credential at the answer.”
open_points.question: Is the prepared request an opaque handle that only service_invoker can inspect, or may effects receive a structure containing the credential value and wire bytes?
options: Return an opaque prepared-request object whose credential and wire representation are inaccessible to effects
Return a plain request structure containing the credential value
Store the prepared request inside service_invoker and return a transient identifier
open_points.default_guess: Return an opaque in-memory prepared-request object accessible only through send_prepared_request.

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list recovery
open_points.text: It must “Return the current token list, re-read when the file changed, or none after a failed re-read,” and “a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes,” but it does not say which digest is retained after an unreadable or invalid configuration.
open_points.question: After a failed re-read, how does the operation detect and accept restoration of the previous valid file bytes, and does it retry an unchanged invalid file on every request?
options: Remember the last observed bytes digest, including invalid content, and retry whenever no valid list exists
Remember only the last valid digest and force a re-read on every request while the list is absent
Remember only the last valid digest and re-read only when bytes differ from it
open_points.default_guess: Remember the last observed digest and also force validation on every request while no valid token list exists.

open_points.subject: classified failure_detail masking
open_points.text: “a classified failure_detail [is returned as] its length and class.”
open_points.question: Is the reported length measured in Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 byte length
Unicode code-point count
Length of the original untruncated service body
open_points.default_guess: Report the UTF-8 byte length of the bounded stored failure_detail.

open_points.subject: get_flow response
open_points.text: get_flow calls “flows.active_flow_version, flows.read_flow_version” but its description only promises “the flow's purpose, its active version and FlowActivation, or that none is active.”
open_points.question: When a flow is active, does get_flow return the complete active FlowVersion graph or only its identity alongside the activation?
options: Return the complete active FlowVersion graph and FlowActivation
Return only the active flow_version_id and FlowActivation
Return summary metadata distinct from both the identity-only and full-graph forms
open_points.default_guess: Return the complete active FlowVersion graph because the catalogue explicitly calls read_flow_version.
